analysis.title: Coffee Break: German office property values hit by rising rates and vacancies
key_insights: German office property prices fell 1.2% yoy in 2Q26, the first decline in six quarters, reflecting higher vacancy rates and rising interest rates.

Office vacancy in Germany's Big 7 cities reached 8.5% as of 1H26, up from 2.9% in 2019. Vacancy has risen since 2020 as working from home cut demand for space. Long-term leases explain the gradual rise.

The 2022 jump in yields from negative levels put heavy pressure on office prices. The 2026 yield increase has been more moderate. Eurozone rates remain higher than at the start of the year despite a recent decline.

Prime rents in core locations are still rising and occupier demand there is strong, while vacancies concentrate in older secondary stock. The report describes a flight to quality that widens the gap between best-in-class and secondary assets.
UniCredit sees no systemic risk for the German banking sector from office loans. It expects more idiosyncratic cases that require higher loan-loss provisions.

1H26 results of German banks active in commercial real estate showed property-specific risks. Some banks reported higher loan-loss provisions and others held provisioning flat yoy. The rise in non-performing loans was driven mainly by office properties.
Vacancy rates are likely to keep rising. Converting obsolete offices into residential units is one way to address office vacancies and housing shortages in major German cities.
AI development adds uncertainty to long-term demand for office space.
US October nonfarm payrolls are expected at about 80k after 29k in September, with the unemployment rate expected to stay at 4.2%. The labour market is described as low-hire, low-fire.

sector_views.rationale: Prices are falling, vacancies are rising and AI adds demand uncertainty. Prime space in core locations remains resilient while secondary stock struggles.
No systemic risk from office loans is expected, but idiosyncratic loan-loss provisions are likely to rise, mainly on office properties.

earnings_insights: German banks active in commercial real estate reported 1H26 results with higher loan-loss provisions at some banks and flat yoy provisioning at others. Non-performing loan increases were driven mainly by office properties.

macro_indicators.interpretation: First yoy decline in six quarters, pointing to pressure on office valuations from vacancies and rates.

macro_indicators.indicator: Office vacancy rate, Big 7 German cities
macro_indicators.interpretation: Up from 2.9% in 2019, and expected to keep rising.
Re-acceleration expected after 29k in September, consistent with a low-hire, low-fire labour market.
Weak September print that sets a low base for October.
Previous reading was 4.2%. Risks come mainly from changes in the participation rate.
Previous reading was 3.0%, so the forecast implies a slight slowdown in wage growth.

risk_factors: Rising vacancy rates in German offices, especially in secondary stock.
Eurozone interest rates remain above their level at the start of the year, pressuring property values.
AI adds long-term uncertainty to office space demand.
Idiosyncratic loan-loss provisions at German banks with office exposure.
Changes in the US labour-force participation rate could move the unemployment rate.

tension_points.bull_case: Prime rents are still rising on persistent demand for high-quality space, and tenants are concentrating on modern, well-located offices in core locations.
tension_points.bear_case: Vacancies keep rising, mainly in secondary stock, prices fell 1.2% yoy in 2Q26, higher rates weigh on valuations and AI adds uncertainty to long-term demand.

theme_stances.key_argument: Rising vacancies and higher rates are lowering office prices, though prime space in core locations holds up.
theme_stances.evidence: prices declined moderately in 1H26, reflecting higher vacancy rates
